title: Companies Act, 2013 — Section 65 (Reserve share capital on conversion)

content.overview: An unlimited company having share capital may, by a resolution for registration as a limited company, increase the nominal amount of each share so the increased capital is callable only on winding up, provide that a specified part of uncalled share capital is callable only on winding up, or do both.
content.glance: An unlimited company having share capital may, by a resolution for registration as a limited company, increase the nominal amount of each share so the increased capital is callable only on winding up, provide that a specified part of uncalled share capital is callable only on winding up, or do both.
content.study: Companies Act, 2013 — Section 65 (Unlimited company to provide for reserve share capital on conversion into limited company). An unlimited company having share capital may, by a resolution for registration as a limited company under the Act, do either or both of the following: (a) increase the nominal amount of its share capital by increasing the nominal amount of each share, subject to the condition that no part of the increased capital may be called up except in the event and for the purposes of winding up; and (b) provide that a specified portion of its uncalled share capital may not be called up except in the event and for the purposes of winding up. The reserve feature is tied to the resolution for registration as a limited company. It is not a general capital-reduction or buy-back procedure.

sections.heading: Eligible company and resolution
sections.body: The company must be an unlimited company having share capital, and the action is taken by a resolution for registration as a limited company under the Companies Act, 2013.

sections.heading: Increase nominal amount of shares
sections.body: The company may increase the nominal amount of its share capital by increasing the nominal amount of each share, provided no part of the increased capital can be called up except in the event and for the purposes of winding up.

sections.heading: Reserve specified uncalled capital
sections.body: The company may provide that a specified portion of its uncalled share capital cannot be called up except in the event and for the purposes of winding up.

sections.heading: Either or both options
sections.body: Section 65 permits the company to choose either or both of the two statutory options in its resolution for registration as a limited company.

provisions.title: Companies Act, 2013 — Section 65: Unlimited company to provide for reserve share capital on conversion into limited company

examples.title: Reserve liability on conversion
examples.body: An unlimited company converting into a limited company may provide, by resolution, that a specified part of uncalled capital shall not be called up except in winding up.

hypotheticals.question: An unlimited company with share capital is registering as a limited company and wants part of its uncalled capital to be callable only on winding up. Is that contemplated by section 65?
hypotheticals.analysis: Yes. Under section 65(b), the resolution for registration as a limited company may provide that a specified portion of uncalled share capital cannot be called up except in the event and for the purposes of winding up.

hypotheticals.question: Must the company choose only one of section 65's options?
hypotheticals.analysis: No. The section permits either or both options: increasing nominal amounts subject to the winding-up limitation and reserving a specified portion of uncalled capital for winding up.

distinctions.title: Reserve share capital on conversion
distinctions.left: Section 65 permits winding-up-only callability of specified capital as part of conversion from unlimited to limited status.
distinctions.right: Sections 66 and 68 govern separate capital-reduction and buy-back procedures.

misconceptions.trap: Describing only a reserve of uncalled capital and omitting the increased-nominal-amount option.
misconceptions.correction: Section 65(a) permits an increase in nominal amount of each share with the increased capital callable only on winding up.

misconceptions.trap: Treating section 65 as a general rule for every limited company.
misconceptions.correction: The section applies to an unlimited company having share capital adopting a resolution for registration as a limited company.

misconceptions.trap: Assuming the reserved capital may be called for ordinary business purposes.
misconceptions.correction: The specified increased or uncalled capital is callable only in the event and for the purposes of winding up.

questionsAndAnswers.question: What options does section 65 permit?
questionsAndAnswers.answer: An unlimited company with share capital may increase the nominal amount of each share with the increased capital callable only on winding up, reserve a specified part of uncalled capital for winding up, or do both.
